reviews.text: Great location near Ximen Station, with clean rooms, nice bathrooms, a quiet environment, a cheap price, and friendly staff. Their elevator is also quite fast. My only slight complaint is that they had a light above the desk that would be dimly lit even with all the switches turned off, making the room not pitch black when you sleep. That’s about it, and was certainly not a dealbreaker.

SCAM - Be Careful – Overpriced 2-Star Hotel (1,030€/1,060$ for 2 Nights) with Low Standards and No Security

Be careful if you’re booking this hotel—especially during holidays! I had to upgrade my room to a family size during New Year’s and was charged an extra 10,000 TWD per night (around 295€ / 315$), even though many rooms were unoccupied. The normal rate for a small room is only 1,200 TWD per night (about 35€ / 38$), making this upgrade ridiculously overpriced for a 2-star hotel in Taiwan.

In total, we paid 35,000 TWD (approximately 1,030€ / 1,060$) for 2 nights, and it turned out to be the most expensive hotel I’ve ever stayed in—despite offering very low standards:
•	No security at the elevators – Anyone could walk in and access any floor without checks.
•	The hotel was old, outdated, and very basic – Definitely not modern.
•	No extra amenities – Except for free coffee from the lobby, which tasted worse than 7-Eleven coffee. There wasn’t even on-site parking; we were told to park nearby.
•	The only positive was that the room was clean—although I still found a hair in the bed after cleaning.

Spending 35,000 TWD (1,030€ / 1,060$) for 2 nights felt like pure exploitation during New Year’s.

For this price, I’ve stayed in 5-star hotels in Europe and Southeast Asia with much better quality and service.

Their normal price is 1,200 TWD per night (about 35€ / 38$), so this upgrade felt like a scam.

I can’t recommend this hotel and hope they at least pay their staff well—but I highly doubt it.

Worst part of this hotel is basic amenities are not met and the hotel falsely advertise online. I was taking shower and after 30 second there was no hot water at all! Hotel also gives you only one key when you are traveling with another person! Lobby also smells disgusting. The whole building smells like old feet. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone! Also hotel asks you to pay cash instead of credit card. This is far the worst hotel in Taipei.

Choose the 11th floor if you choose to stay here. I got the room #1103. It was good with bath tub. The room rate was reasonable.

reviews.text:
amazing value for money. the best dorm type accommodation i have ever stayed in by FAR. large cubicle with a double bed for 1pax, sufficient locker spaces, friendly international staff, comfortable, clean, nice common area, laundry room, and comes with a pretty decent breakfast buffet.

5min walk to raohe night market, and a very self-sufficient neighbourhood with a 7-11 just across the road, as well as cafes, bars, and eateries nearby. not the most central location BUT honestly at this standard it is hardly a drawback.

love the place :-) been there 2 times now. If you've booked one of the luxury rooms on the upper floors ask for the ones with balcony facing towards 101, the views are stunning. But also the rooms on the opposite side offer great outlooks over northern Taipei. The luxury rooms are kept in a decent individual style. The cozy lobby area is a good place to unwind and meet other fellow travellers. It has a practical kitchen with some chairs and tables and also a small outside balcony to relax with a drink or a having a smoke. If you are after some comfort but still like the backpacker-feeling this is definitely an excellent choice in Taipei.

This was probably the cleanest hostel I've ever stayed in. The staff were super great, the beds were comfortable, and the free breakfast was fantastic. Paid $45ish Canadian for a double bed in a 10 bed dorm. Room mates were all very quiet and respectful.

5-10 minute walk to train station and bustling night market.

Rented a room for a week. A bit noisy with a fan in the ceiling that makes a lot of noise. Ceiling also leaking water when it rains. Good with laundry facilities on a separate floor. Front desk staff aren’t very service minded. They charge NTD 400 / hour for late checkout. Breakfast quality very low. Close to good breakfast stands in the neighborhood. Excellent WiFi.

As hostels go, this would be the executive level. Beds are double size. Full breakfast every morning, starting at 7AM till 10AM or 30 minutes later on weekends. There is a rotation in food items every day, with hard boiled eggs, rice congee, stir fried noodles, dumplings, Taiwanese sliced ham or sausages. In addition to vegetables, salad and canned tuna fish. Coffee, soy milk or orange drink (not real juice).

The dorm rooms are spacious and individual lockers are full size and the shower facility is pretty good. Towels are provided.

The main common area is on the fifth floor with a secondary common area on the eighth. Both common areas have a full kitchen however if one wants to lounge, the eighth floor has the sofas.

As an executive hostel, guests here are predominantly locals who may be working in Taipei, while their families live elsewhere. There is a small Western presence.

The other floors consist of regular hotel rooms and aside from breakfast, there is little interaction with them. The majority of the guests there would be tourists from Hong Kong or other families seeking a reasonably priced stay in the area.

Overall an excellent bang for the buck.

The only drawback would be related to the building's heating system, which pumps out air at 80% humidity. As this would likely be a global control, towels and other clothes do not dry well.

As for me, being only one block away from Roahe Night Market is what led me to discover this hidden gem.

Don't worry about the PIN to your lockers. Heh there is a master reset key with reception.

reviews.text: Just what I needed after 5 weeks traveling Asia. The in room spring fed tub was a godsend. I barely left my room. The staff was welcoming and it was an incredible value compared to all the hotels nearby. Cool trails to walk right outside the door, 5 min walk to the closest train. I will definitely go back.

Here's a 5-star hotel review for the Grand Pleasure Spring Hotel in Taipei:

*5/5 Stars: Blissful Retreat with Exceptional Service*

My family and I had the pleasure of staying at the Grand Pleasure Spring Hotel in Taipei, and it was truly an unforgettable experience. This hidden gem exceeded our expectations in every way.

*Room Highlight: Private Hot Spring Tub*

Our room featured a luxurious private hot spring tub, perfect for relaxing and rejuvenating. The water quality was exceptional, and the tranquil ambiance made us feel like we were in a serene oasis.

Exceptional Staff

The staff at Grand Pleasure Spring Hotel were outstanding – professional, friendly, and fluent in English. They went above and beyond to accommodate our needs, particularly when we needed to switch rooms to extend our stay. They graciously allowed us extra time in our initial room and seamlessly transferred us to our new accommodation, assisting with our luggage.

Neighborhood Charm

The hotel's surroundings are picturesque, offering a tranquil escape from Taipei's bustling streets.

Standout Features:

- Private hot spring tub in-room
- Excellent, English-speaking staff
- Accommodating and helpful service
- High-quality hot spring water
- Beautiful neighborhood

Recommendation

If you're seeking a relaxing retreat with top-notch service, look no further than Grand Pleasure Spring Hotel. We can't wait to return!

Tips:

- Take advantage of the hotel's relaxing hot spring facilities
- Explore the charming neighborhood

I had been looking for a budget friendly hot spring hotel in a central location Beitou but was at a loss until I came across Grand Pleasure Spring Hotel. The decor is a charming older style that is well maintained and the hot spring bath in the room is amazing! Will definitely stay again when I visit Beitou.

Quiet location away from the hustling and bustling but still well within walking distance from the subway.  Roomy and clean room with private hot spring tub for soaking anytime of the day.  Excellent place for a very reasonable price.

The private onsen inside the room is indeed quite nice, although the water temp tops out at only 102F, and it takes at least 20 min to get an amount of water you can sit in.

I really enjoyed the location, but I enjoy walking up and down hills, and it is a lot of that.  It was a good balance where you could easily walk downhill to downtown Beitou, and also easily walk or go for a run uphill to some of the nicer nature places like thermal valley, Yangmingshan park, and the rock climbing area.

Room wise, bed was chintzy and way too easy to move around unintentionally, headboard wasn’t attached to the wall either and would just fall down if the bed moved too far.  I guess I’m saying it’s not great for couples with an “active” relationship.  Mattress and pillows were comfy though.

I think we stayed about a week?  I think it’s a good value at the weekday rates, but not really getting what you’re paying for when it goes to 6-10k.

reviews.text: As a couple we really appreciate the double bed. We also had stairs not a ladder to the top bunk. Everything is nice and clean. Can walk to main station and various places in Taipei. Would recommend.

Nice place with an affordable price. Loved the basement dinner area. Very large and tidy. Bedroom and bathroom are clean.

Only that if we want to rent items, they should be returned during operating hours which is 10 am otherwise your deposit will not be returned.

We had fun at the Inn during our 3 nights in Taipei. We met a lot of nice people there. Staff was very friendly. We had a couple of problems in the room (defunct AC, clogged toilet), which they promptly fixed and the rooms were otherwise in quite good shape for a hostel. The stairs up to the upper bunk bed was also much better than a ladder that you would usually have. The common area in the basement was spacious and you could meet a lot of people there, but it was not very clean but still ok. They also have electric dehumidifiers in each room, which is great.

I’m travelling 1 months in Taiwan and it was definitely the worst hostel I’ve been in here.
The room is too small. You feel like you don’t have privacy at all, and not even enough space for bags. You get to hear everything that going on with your roommates, and if you didn’t have luck and had roommate that snores, you will probably not sleep all night. There is only one bathroom in the room, it’s dirty and smells awful. Everything you might ask is extra charge.
The price is much more expensive than it is really worth.
I would definitely will not recommend go there.

Stayed there with my 5 of my friends and it was a nice place to stay. I would recommend this if you are travelling with a group so you'll have the whole room to yourselves than sharing it with others. Cheap compared to other hostels.

The only thing I can hate is that the stairs going to the elevator if you have a heavy luggage to carry nonetheless this is a nice place to stay.

reviews.text:
I stayed for 2 nights. I think their double room is perfect for solo, might be too small for 2 people. The room was a little smelly but I bought air fresheners at Watsons nearby.
The wifi for the rooms is different from the wifi at the lobby so make sure you check the sign in your room for your network so you get the best connection.
The location of this hotel is the best feature. Lots of really good food nearby and a Daiso. You can easily find the hotel by exiting from M6 from Taipei main station and walking straight.
There is only 1 plug by the bed which is used by the minibar and 2 USB outlets. I unplugged the minibar so I could use the outlet for my charger.

I book the hostel to stay just for a day. It's cheap and really convenient location. Connected to Taipei Main station, the room and bathroom is just fine. Not bad but not very comfortable. But considering the price, it's nothing to complain :)

This hostel has a great location, it’s very close to the Taipei Main Station and close to the touristy places.

The service was okay, but the room was quite dark and stuffy. And there were no basic amenities like a microwave, washing machine and refrigerator. No towel as well, and there is no place to hang your wet towel.

What more else can I say?? It's just a few minutes walk to Taipei Main Station closest exit/entrance is Z2 just a straight away at the entrance and past the (temporary) shopping stalls.

Anyway it's all just a few walk from everything!!!

Front of the entrance is a department store, across the road there's Uniqlo, NET shop, Daiso, Japanese sushi, McDonald's, Starbucks, and other cafes. A few walk and turn from either left or right are massage salons, Bank of Taiwan, local cafes you can have your breakfast, and many more.

Even if the room has no window, it's still great place to stay. Although walls may be thin you can hear someone's taking a shower on the next room but still it's still recommendable. Before I requested for room cleaning, the toilet room smelled a bit moldy and after cleaning it's great. Towels are also provided and there's shampoo and bath soap already in the toilet. There's also a mini fridge, hair blower, and a secret room 🤭.

Overall my stay here in Taipei Inn is great. Will definitely book here again!

Although this is a convenient location, I would not recommend this accommodation as we stayed in other areas during our trip and had much better value for money. We booked a private room with a bathroom during our stay and it smelled like smoke even though it is a non-smoking establishment. There were several small lights you couldn’t turn off in the room, ants in the bathroom, and the walls are very thin so we could hear conversations in the room next to us. We decided to move for our second night because the smoke smell was too much.

Good pressure in the shower, but you do have to wait for hot water. And toilette sit is extra cold (never experienced anything like it before). Bring your own slippers. No problems with the carpet in the room. Nice that they have extra blankett in the wardrobe. Would have loved to stay more days.

Our room was so terrible.  The room had moisture problem which is why a dehumidifier was in our room (and very full).  I think the whole floor had a moisture problem because there dehumidifier in the hallways too.   It’s winter so it was kinda windy and cool outside.  Out heater never worked, so we ended up pretty cold all night.  We turned it on and set the settings correctly.   We called the front desk but they didn’t really understand the problem.

So heater and cooling central air system seemed broken and only had a fan mode.  The room smelled like little like old cigarettes but I could figure out from where (maybe the vent which central heating/cooling / fan is connected to another smoking room or something).

We had a cheaper room but it was ridiculous bad for this price.  The furniture seem like all super old furniture from different homes and very mid matched.  It didn’t fit the room space well.

To be honest this was overpriced and very uncomfortable.  I will not be staying in this hotel again for this area.

Also the lobby smells like old stale popcorn.  I guess some people like that smell but to me kinda smells bad.

The hotel is great! It’s located near Fisherman’s Wharf, easy walking distance.
I stayed in Classic Double Room and I could see the sunset from my room.
The hotel staff were helpful and friendly. I very much enjoyed my stay.

What a lovely hotel; short walking distance to the fisherman's wharf; convienent stores and the bus stop. The rooms were clean and fresh; beds were comfy. Water supply pressure was good. I love the welcome pack of snacks and drinks in the room. By the reception area, they have an area with a coffee machine, South African Rooibos tea, other drinks and a variety of snacks, which are available 24hrs for you to enjoy. * Their hotel slippers were really nice. I even kept my pair to use at home. Breakfast buffet was enough. Asian style as well as toasts, cereals and fruit. Umbrellas are also available to use at the entrance which comes in handy. Overall it was a really lovely, welcoming stay. One that deserves another visit ;) Thank you Fisher Hotel

Good hotel, friendly receptionist, with beautiful scenery of wharf. We are really enjoy our double ten holiday in this hotel. Maybe, if they want to make varied breakfast, it would be perfect for guest. Thank you.

All in all it’s an affordable and nice place if your not fussy!

Rooms are great as well. Very clean and modern. Good views 👍🏽

Tomorrow Hotel is a fantastic choice for travelers looking for convenience and comfort. Its location is unbeatable—right near the city and close to the best spots in Taipei, making it perfect for exploring.

The staff are incredibly nice and helpful, adding to the overall pleasant experience. The rooms are clean, simple, and straightforward, providing everything you need for a comfortable stay. Plus, it’s very accessible and budget-friendly, making it a great option for travelers. Highly recommended!

The location is excellent, just a 1-minute walk from the MRT.

I was "upgraded" from a windowless room to one with a window, but the window was small and faced a concrete wall.

The window didn't block noise from a party downstairs, which kept me awake till 3am!

The room has no soundproofing. I could hear everything from the neighboring room, including conversations, shower time and more.

The double bed was two single beds pushed together.

The "upgrade" included a dirty bathtub that made the bathroom constantly wet.

The room was dusty and had hair everywhere.

I was asked to give a 5-star Google review at check-in for free coffee, cake, and ice cream. I'm glad I didn't, as the review would have been dishonest. The hotel is not 5-star.

Wonderful Stay and Excellent Service!

I had an amazing stay at Tomorrow Hotel. The staff was incredibly welcoming, the rooms were spotless and comfortable, and the amenities were top-notch. The location was perfect, and the on-site restaurant served delicious meals. I highly recommend this hotel and would definitely stay here again!

reviews.text:
I stayed at this hotel in Taipei and had a good experience overall. The location is very convenient, just about 300 meters from Taipei Main Station. The staff were friendly and helpful—I was even upgraded to a bigger room, which I really appreciated.

The room was clean and equipped with all the necessary amenities. The breakfast was simple, like a standard hotel breakfast, but if you prefer to eat out, there are plenty of cafes, brunch spots, and breakfast places nearby.

One thing to note is that the walls are quite thin, so you can hear noise from both neighboring rooms and outside, especially since the hotel is close to a major transportation hub. However, it was still acceptable for me, and the hotel provides earplugs for guests.

Overall, it was a pleasant stay, and I would consider staying here again.

We stayed here for three nights. On the first night, we arrived very late, but the hotel was easy to find, located not far from Taipei Main Station. Despite the late hour, the reception staff was fully prepared to serve us and even upgraded our room.

We liked that the bathroom had a bidet spray, and the shampoo and shower gel smelled nice. Although we could hear some noise from the floor above or from the street, it wasn't bothersome at all. We slept very comfortably, probably because we had been walking around sightseeing all day and were tired enough to fall asleep quickly.

As for breakfast, there was a good variety of food options.

Mold.

This hotel could go up a whole star by simply replacing the moldy shower curtains.

My room did not have an AC or heat unit. There was a remote for a heater but no heater.

My two cents when looking for hotels in Taipei: don't get hung up on free breakfast or free coffee. There are 7-11's surrounding this hotel and 100+ choices for dining. You do not need to book your hotel based on free breakfast.

We are Muslim travelers from Malaysia, consisting of two adult women and one teenage girl. We chose this hotel because of its proximity to Taipei Main Station and its designation as a Muslim-friendly hotel with complimentary breakfast. Upon arrival, we were frequently greeted by fellow Malaysian travelers. Our stay of four nights went smoothly without any major issues.

For the first three nights, we stayed in a room with three single beds. However, the space was quite limited, making it uncomfortable. There was barely any room for prayer, so we had to push the beds together to create some space. On the last night, we moved to a room with one queen bed and one single bed, which felt more comfortable, even though the room size appeared to be the same.

The hotel’s definition of “Muslim-friendly” includes providing a Qibla direction marker in the room and a bidet in the bathroom. However, while the hotel stated that daily room cleaning was provided, we noticed that our beds were not made, nor were the bed linens changed throughout our stay. Only basic services such as replenishing bottled water, changing towels, and replacing floor mats were provided.

As for breakfast, we do not recommend it for Muslim travelers since the hotel also serves pork, making it unsuitable for Muslims. Instead, travelers can look for halal food options nearby or purchase vegetarian or tuna onigiri from nearby convenience stores. The nearest halal restaurant is Chang Halal Beef Noodles, but we advise checking its operating hours on Google before visiting.

For those arriving at the hotel via MRT, the closest exit is Exit Z10. However, please note that Exit Z10 is located at the far end of the station, requiring quite a bit of walking. Additionally, it only has stairs, so if you are carrying heavy luggage, pushing a stroller, or using a wheelchair, it is advisable to consider an alternative exit.

We stayed here for 6 nights. It's a decent and clean hotel. We were properly greeted and the checked in process was fast. We emailed earlier regarding our extra pax (2 kids) and they answered us properly via email indicating the extra charges that we have to pay upon arrival. Staffs were nice and helpful.
This is a Muslim friendly hotel. They provided Muslim prayer time and Qiblah direction in the room. About the breakfast buffet, they properly marked menu with pork so that we can identify easily. Since we are practicing Muslim, the only item we can eat every morning was bread with spread of butter/peanut butter/jam. We could not eat other dishes prepared for example like the fried potato/vegetable and cut fruits as we knew it was cooked using the same utensils for dishes with pork. Anyhow,we appreciate the kitchen staffs kind gestures explaining to us about their dishes. For future improvement, maybe the hotel can get more information about halal food and how it is prepared. For example, the staff tell us to eat the Mantau bread in the steam basket with pork dim sum at the lower rack of the steam basket. We understand that this is not a fully halal hotel and therefore we just declined politely.
Clean towels were provided daily and they did the housekeeping daily too. Taipei Main Train station dan local bus stop is just a walking distance from the hotel. We also love the massage centre located very near to the hotel. We had a great late night massage before resting in hotel. Generally, this is a recommended hotel.

reviews.text:
There are too many negatives to recommend Hotel Leisure Tamsui / Life Hotel for the Tamsui district:

The WiFi is extremely unstable, constantly logging on and off and resetting during our two-night stay.

There is only ONE electrical outlet in the entire room, and it is an old-style two-prong plug. All the light fixtures in our room were hardwired to the wall, making it impossible to find more outlets. However, I was able to receive on loan a multi-outlet from front-desk.

Coffee and tea were provided, but there was no creamer or sugar. The breakfast dining area also lacked sugar for coffee. There is no doubt either the hotel operators not drinking coffee personally or only drank water down coffee as one finds in many older established eateries in Taiwan.

Breakfast options cater to local tastes, so be prepared for this limitation.

Check-in time is strictly at 4 PM, with no exceptions. I highly suggest the hotel operators travel more to understand how hospitality works.

The exterior of the hotel and public areas are modern, giving the impression of an upscale atmosphere. However, like many places in Taiwan, the interior is chaotic and neglected. The room was outdated, reflecting its downward budget pricing. The room is what one finds from 1970s Taipei time, bare minimum and mismatching of furnishing and decorations.

The hotel's location from Tamsui station requires a walk on a narrow and broken sidewalk, uphill. The path to the hotel is as terrible as the guest rooms.

The staff is average, meeting but not exceeding expectations. Perhaps with better experience outside of this facility, they could improve.

Now, I'm trying to comprehend the numerous positive reviews of the hotel. I wonder if these reviews are genuinely from guests or if they are fabricated by forced labor in an undisclosed location in Thailand.

BEST saving grace of the facility is the cleanliness of smoke or mold odor typically of numerous local hotels.

The hotel is up the hill from Tamsui station.  It's close enough to walk down, but not good for multiple trips.  The hotel was a luxury hotel when it was built, but is showing its age.  Comfortable and clean.  A good hotel, not great.

Overall a good stay, walking distance to tamsui old street or take 1 bus stop to tamsui MRT. Clean and spacious room, new hotel therefore things are still new, acceptable breakfast, friendly services, service crews always greet with smiles. A bit sad as seven eleven was closed during our stay for upgrading.
Very noisy, room 709 has zero sound insulation. Not only that, heavy trucks and extra loud motorcycles cause vibrations.
It's clean and tidy. No carpet. Have a bar table and high chairs. However, the temperature of hot water for shower is not stable.

reviews.text: The room is okay and the room was clean, modern, and comfortable. The hotel offers great amenities, and the location was ideal for sightseeing. It really felt like great value for the price.  I loved how quiet and relaxing the environment was. Highly recommend it for anyone looking for a peaceful and enjoyable stay.

This hotel is about a 10-minute walk from Taipei Main Station, which I found to be a convenient location. Check-in is available anytime via a self-service machine, and there is also a pickup/drop-off service.

The twin room was spacious enough for two people, and the Wi-Fi worked well. Hot water was also reliable. However, I did notice some stains on the bed.

Overall, considering the price, I was satisfied with my stay

It's actually a very good place!

The average price of hotels in Taipei is quite high with small space, that's my conclusion after searching for hotels here. So be prepared that rooms in Taipei will be small and that's normal. I travel with 2 other friends and they stayed at another hotel with same price, to be honest, the room there was also small, even not as cozy and beautiful as here.

I got a single bed room, and the experience after 3 nights are:

Pros:
- cozy, bed and pillow are soft and comfortable
- the room is designed to utilize space, you can put the luggages under the bed, and there are still space to walk
- the hot water in faucet is steady, you don't have to adjust the temperature all the time while you take shower (like most hotels I stayed before)
- room and bathroom are super clean, and they make up room everyday
- room and facilities are new

Cons:
- no bidet shower
- wall is thin, I was lucky that the next room keep quiet, only hear the door closing. But if they talk much, you might need to prepare ear plug
- no laundry service
Very clear instruction for self check-in/check-out. We had a very good night sleep due to comfy beds and silent rooms. Attendant in the hotel lobby is so kind and speaks English very well!

Stayed for a night after landing in Taipei. It's a short walk from Taipei main station, easy to find. I arrived late night, check-in was smooth and easy. The room is equipped with basics necessities. It has no windows, but is clean and comfortable for me as a solo traveller. Staff at the front desk was helpful when I ask about info getting around the area and typhoon situation. There's a park nearby that is lovely. Recommended for a quick stopover in Taipei!

reviews.text:
The Cheapest Hotel Option in a Prime Location

Pros: The room is a decent size, and the location is excellent (just a 3-minute walk to Zhongshan Junior High School MRT station).

Cons: The bathroom feels run-down, with rust and gaps in the shower. The check-in and check-out process is entirely self-service, and there are no staff members on-site. The room also has poor sound isolation, so you can hear noise from other guests and outside.

Useless hotel—don’t waste your time. I arrived at the hotel at 00:30 AM. There was no one at reception, and my code from Booking.com didn’t work. As a result, I couldn’t check in through the machine and had to find another hotel in the middle of the night.

Located about a 5 minute walk from Zhongshan Junior High School MRT station, this small hotel is cheap and a good place for you to spend the night here! Stayed here for 1 night from 7 - 8 January 2025. We came here 3 hours ahead of check in time [3pm], so we came back at 4pm after visiting Taipei 101, placing our luggage bags in the designated area for luggages provided. Checked in using the smart screen. I'm quite impressed at first glance by the hotel room itself.

Our room was on the 6th floor, and the room itself was really spacious, for 4 people! The bathroom itself consisted of a toilet, and a separate glass panel separating the shower and bath itself. However, weird thing, the sink was outside of the bathroom, next to the bed. Quite an unusual setup if I do say myself. Also, half of the switches in the room don't work for some reason. You gotta trial & error which switch turns off or on the correct light. Plugs are not international friendly, so you've gotta bring their local adaptor type. But, the study table itself was quite big, and the light above makes it good for work!

View wasn't the best but at least we could open the window to get some cooling air! Beds were decent, and there was a television that supported YouTube, Spotify casting and even Disney+. They also had an international weather forecast showing famous cities in the world, but it's really inaccurate. They displayed Singapore as 17 degrees and Hong Kong as -1 degree. The only correct ones were Taipei and some cities in Europe, but the TV was great! This hotel is also located a 8 minute walk away from McDonald's, and 2 minutes away from the local 7-11!

Overall, it's a decent hotel for a cheap price! There's no amenities itself in the hotel like lounges or breakfast etc., but the rooms are great for the price!

You'll have a big chance of staying in a room where you'll hear noises like people are moving furniture around at midnight.
They won't provide earplugs

The employees don't stand by at front desk.  When emergency , you can't find help.  😖    The hotel obviously don't train their employees professionally . The employees show indifference towards guests' needs and talked back to guests.  The television of my first-day stay was broken.  Their phones only work for calling front desk , not for calling outside. They use the excuses of  undergoing remodeling, but as far as I know it has been under new management for a few years. If you are from overseas visiting Taiwan, I suggest that you not stay here.  The only positive is their location , for all the other aspects, 😖😖😖😖😖

reviews.text: Ivy, Lee and Chen are always very friendly and very good people in reception. Best hostel in Taipei. Always clean and comfortable place to stay and a great price. Close to everything you need.

Only 4.1 stars? I'd give it 5.1 stars if I could!

I've been to a fair few hostels around the world and this is honestly the BEST hostel I've ever been to! (No that's not cut & pasted:)

The staff are so sweet and sincere. No superficiality or impatience like in some other hostels.  I even played the staff a little concert in the reception and they offered me cake.  It felt like a friends reunion 💃🎶🕺

The common room downstairs is also the best I've seen.  Huge Chillout room / Workspace.with lots of tables and comfy sofas.

All the other amenities are tip top and it's close to lots of great local street cafes where you can have a big meal for around 2-3USD and breakfast for under 2USD!

So thanks Ivy, Chen & Lee for making my stay feel like a home away from home ❤️🏠🌻

So come with a smile and enjoy😀

Comfortable and clean place, with a convenient location only 15 min walk from the main station. The dorm rooms and bathrooms are a bit small, and the lockers can only fit personal items, so there's not much room for backpacks or suitcases, but it's a good value for money. I liked the spacious and cozy common area.

Excellent location. Only 10-15 mins walking from Taipei Main Station.

About 3 mins walking to the nearest FamilyMart.

This is not party hostel. If you are seeking quiet, peaceful sleep, this place is for you.

There are curtains on the beds for more privacy. Laundry is available. The LG Level has a dining area. They can also keep your luggage after check out until 9PM.

No cockroaches or bed bugs. Comfy beds. Lockers inclusive. Luggage storage. Good location. Clean and working toilet plus bathroom. What more can a traveller ask for?
Good location near Taipei main station. Exit Y13. Great for a short stay overnight if you need to catch a train somewhere the next morning.

reviews.text: My family stayed here from Sep 10 - 14, 2024. Clean room, comfortable shower pressure, amazing front desk services. Arrived 7 am and way too early for check in. Free checked bags. Loved the continental breakfast.

The hotel is super clean. The staff are very supportive and friendly. In my last trip, I left some stuff at the hotel and went back to Vietnam. The hotel staff managed to send the clothes to my address in Vietnam which was incredible. I’m so grateful to her help. 5 star service!

This is my first time in Taiwan and I have to do a 3+4 quarantine and self prevention schedule. I amazed seeing the rooms are so neat and clean especially the washroom. They provided everything you require to stay for 8 nights. The staffs are always on time in providing meals, replying your queries through Line(at late night too) or any other issues. At first, my room was facing the back alley, so there was no sunlight at all. I just told them about it and requested to change my room. They did it without any hassle. Now, my room has a big window(almost half of the wall) facing the front,full of sunlight. One day, I informed them to off my dinner, they quickly provided me a fruit box. I was so touched. Overall, my experience is very good with this hotel. If you are searching for isolation hotel, you can definitely check this one.

Pretty good value, the hotel's a bit dated but room was spacious and clean. Service however was lacking, we asked for cleaning twice in the mornings and even wrote down our room number at reception, but the cleaner never came. Upon checkout the front desk agent demanded that we each leave a 5 star review, and hovered over us to see that we complied. For the price we paid though, we'd consider it again

For the price and a last-minute booking, I felt the room was worth the stay for a solo traveller. The location is decent as well, there is a direct bus to the airport. Service is good, staff are there 24/7 and they will keep your luggage for you (even on the checkout day). Do keep in mind it is a rather old hotel but the rooms are spacious and clean. What you may want to consider are the beds - mattresses may not be long enough for you if you are taller than the average Taiwanese. I also found them a bit hot to sleep in because of the thick duvet, so bring light clothes (and conditioner). The rooms are non-smoking rooms.

Definitely clean

Will definitely stay here again in Taipei 👌

It's fine if you want a cheap place to stay for a night or two, but a friend and i had a few nights and wasnt easy to walk around in that tiny room with our luggages covering pretty much all of the remaining floor.

Cleanliness was alright though they really need some maintenance. The sockets i had were sunken into the wall making it a bit inconvenient to plug in. The slight dust and mould on the edges of the walls and toilet could do some work. The one that really had me worried was the socket and hair dryer just at the edge of the shower with no curtain.

Though tucked away in an alley, location is good, convenience stores and shopping just outside along the main road.

I'm not saying it's a horrible place, just needs some work.

Can check in on 15:00 onward. The hotel allows you to drop your luggage at the hotel before check in, quite convenient. Room was super small. Not recommend for couple or family. This is not a place for spend a romantic night for you😅.

The location of this hotel is perfect, it is a short walk from Ximen station and Ximending which is full of shops and eateries. The breakfast they provide during our stay was congee with a bunch of savoury assortments which was tasty and a great way to fill you up to get you on your day (they also offer toast, jam, butter, coffee and tea).

The wet room was clean and our room was cleaned every day and we came home to fresh towels too even if we didn't leave our room until 1pm. The TV had a good selection of channels in mandarin, Korean and English.

The front desk is manned 24 hours a day and they were very friendly and helpful.

My faults with the hotel are that although understandably the rooms are small apart from 2 large shelves above the TV there wasn't anywhere else to hang your clothes. They did provide a bar with a few hangers but this was pretty pointless once clothes were actually on it. A few hooks on the wall would have been better.

There was also always the stale smell of cigarette smoke once we left the lift and walked into the hallway. This is a none smoking hotel and I saw signs everywhere stating this and whilst I was there I didn't see anyone smoke so I have no idea where the smell was from.

A major issue for me is that the doors are very thin. Any activity happening in the hallway might as well be inside your room. We even heard our neighbouring room guest shouting at people talking on their phone in the hallway at night.

The room is a tad small, however I picked it up for a cheap price. The hotel is in a fairly good locations with plenty of shops and night market around. It's also roughly a 10 min walk to the subway, making it fairly favourable for someone new to Taipei.

However, it was a good location. You can walk 20 minutes to the nearest night market. There are also lots of stalls nearby so its not too shabby. We picked this hotel because we had a 13 hour layover, so we needed to be near the airport, and it was 20 minutes away from airport so it was good enough.

We got the quadruple room and the room was big but has some smell, aircon was working. Shower heater working as well but no bidet. Overall hotel was okay for its price.
You should just get an AirBNB. The "queen sized" bed is two twins pushed together and both the bed and pillows are HARD.

Very mediocre hotel to stay in, location is good as it is near the city, the staff here was really kind and attentive. reviews.text:
A bit far from the main station. There’s a bus that takes you close to the hostel from the main station, but it took me a long time to find the right one since the bus stops are quite spread out, so make sure to budget time for that.

The bedding was very basic. Rickety bunk bed with a ladder for the top bunk that’s right in the middle of the entry way for the bottom bunk. The mattress was thin so not great if you’re a side sleeper. The lights allocated for each bunk leaks through the bunks, so it’s tough to get to sleep earlier than your bunk mate if they leave their light on.

Bathrooms were clean. The toilet and shower stalls in the ladies bathroom were very narrow, but I suppose that’s to be expected for a city. They have an accessible bathroom.

The pillow is so flat and you have to put the duvet cover by yourself which is very inconvenient! I booked a dormitory room with 14beds but ended up in a small dormitory with very narrow pathway. The location of this hostel is good tho since it's near the metro.

Good hostel. The private room is small but comfortable. The bathroom is big but cold in the winter.

400m from metro station. ChiaTe pineapple cake store is nearby.

Staff is nice and helpful.

Comfortable hostel near the MRT station in Taipei. Stayed for three nights in July 2017. The air conditioning was strong in the rooms, but was almost nonexistent in the laundry room (was a it weaker in the kitchen as well). Staff were friendly and spoke English.

Come across this place when I was looking for an affordable stay nearby Taipei Arena. Love this hostel. They provide a great service, facility and strategic location. You can get here by MRT or bus, which located so close to the hostel. Bike is also available for rental. Will definitely come back again when I’m back for another Taipei Arena event.

reviews.text: Design is outdated. Floor and toilet door are stained and old. Toilet has a strange smell to it. What bothered us the most is the thin walls! We could clearly hear people watching TV next door and there is a site construction next to the hotel. They were working evening on Sunday! Aircon and water heater are working fine though. Location is ok, but not near train station.

Le Room was easy to find and also really convenient to get to Ximending for a very affordable price. The lobby was spacious and well-equipped with chairs, snacks, electrical appliances etc. However, the rooms looked quite different from the pictures. They were quite dated (eg. Bathtub is more yellowish in colour than white, and there were stains, tap felt a bit sticky). The rooms were definitely on the smaller side. There wasn’t space for us to open both of our luggages, and when we did, nobody could walk in the room, and this made packing tricky for two of us. We were assigned the room on the second floor, right next to the lift. It was located along the road so there were definitely sounds from the in/out movements, traffic. The floor also felt “sticky”, so we had to put on the slippers that they gave.

We stayed for a night so we didn’t bother with any feedback because we just wanted to crash for the night and leave. It definitely wasn’t the most comfortable stay for us, and what you pay is really what you get.

The front desk was really responsive though. I accidentally left my bolster behind and emailed them about it. They quickly replied and I could pick it up when I went back to Taipei so that was helpful :)

VERY BAD!! this hotel is the worst. The service was really bad, we got scammed. False advertisement in a platform they use to sell hotel rooms, and decided to blame it on THE PLATFORM. That's abruptly wrong since the owner is the one that put the picture NOT THE PLATFORM. The bathroom was dirty and rusty, there are a lot of reviews about the cleanliness and the owner doesn't seem to reply to any of it. But only replies about the others. The air vent WAS REALLY RUSTY. I have a proof that it was rusty. Not too mention, the receptionist stares at us like a crazy person. THEY WERE EXTREMELY RUDE TOO? We have explained it throughly about our room problems but they don't seem to care about it and blame it to someone else. The bed was stained, The towel was stained. How could you leave it like that! That's absolutely disgusting. The room smell was absurd. The smell of dust, rust, mold combined together. Please for the future customer, see the recent reviews before booking this hotel. Unless you wanna get scammed with a uncleanness hotel room with rude staffs. The location was the only thing good there. DO NOT COME HERE. I WARN YOU.

Before booking this hotel, please read the recent reviews as they are more accurate given the current state of the hotel.

Staff are not friendly and they are ALWAYS on their phones playing games or watching youtube videos using the company’s desktop 🤡. They don’t bother greeting guests or even look up to the guests and smile as they are busy entertaining themselves on phone and on the computer. Whenever guests (including myself) approach them for any issues, they are always reluctant to provide help and act as if we are disrupting their game/show 🤣. Sometimes they are even seen sleeping at the receptionist desk which is very unprofessional considering that this is their working hours. Oh also, they don’t even have a proper set of uniform.

Room is pathetically small and dusty. Toilet seat in room 605 is completely broken and detached. Room’s insulation is super bad. You will be able to hear the water sounds whenever your neighbours are showering and you can even hear their conversations. Don’t be fooled by those images you see online.

And when you request for room makeover, you will only get clean trash cans, new sets of toiletries, new bottles of water and towels. Your bed will still be messy, sheets will not be changed and floor will not be cleaned, no matter how many days you will be staying.

The hotel is also currently undergoing renovations so it will definitely disrupt your sleep if you do not intend to wake up at 7am every morning as it is super loud. On top of that, there are also constructions going on right opposite the hotel, so you can already roughly imagine the noise you will be hearing early in the morning. Free alarm clock i guess 🤡

The hotel also overcharge taxi services. You’re better off booking taxis on uber or just simply flag one outside. Guarantee that it will be cheaper and faster.

Also, with this price, you are also able to get a better deal in Ximending area that are nearer to the MRT. You can even get better deals at a cheaper price, just have to scroll a little bit more and read a couple more of reviews. 100% would never recommend this hotel to anyone. Super bad experience overall. Didn’t even want to give it 1 star to be frank. The only good thing i could think about of this hotel is that the breakfast place located right opposite the building is good, thats all 🤣

There goes my first experience posting a bad review on Google.

I have recently quarantined here and the service has been excellent. The room is spacious enough to do exercises, the facilities provided work well, with fantastic water pressure in the shower. The bed is comfortable and large, which is definitely appreciated. The team working here are extremely responsive on LINE, and have no issues with any requests you might have (topping up on coffee, etc). I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone!

reviews.text: The hostel is in a great location with plenty of food options nearby. However, the WiFi is very slow, both in the rooms and the lounge. The locker placement is inconvenient—it’s at the farthest corner of the pod, requiring you to step on the bed to access it. Unpacking is also a hassle since you have to place your luggage on the bed to reach the locker. The room itself feels extremely depressing and quiet, offering zero privacy despite the curtain, as every small noise is noticeable. For the price, it’s okay if you don’t mind sacrificing comfort.

Possibly the worst hotel I've stayed in Taiwan. This is my 5th trip to Taiwan and I cannot recommend this place. They don't make your room until very late in the evening. I am writing this review close to 5PM sitting in the lobby waiting for the room to be cleaned.
The pillows had a strange smell.
The wifi is erratic and not consistent at all.
Breakfast is not on premises and you have to walk to another restaurant where you can choose from a selection of tiny sandwiches.
Just 2 bath towels with no hand towels. I've stayed in better places at lesser cost in Taiwan. Stay away from here.

I thought I should add this as well. Finally got into the room at around 6 PM. Wifi which was not writing when I left in the morning is still not working. The guy at the reception said he will do something about it but nothing has changed.

Worst hotel I’ve ever stay in, like seriously. First, the rooms are SO SMELLY! The ventilation or something about it seriously sucks. Smells full of sweat. Worst is that nobody bothers cleaning the toilet. It smells like pee all the time, both the shower and the toilet. They’re ultra small too for the info, you’ll literally feel claustrophobic when using them. Sucks, really really sucks. Staff’s attitude is extremely bad, like you owe them billions. Treats you rudely and speaks to u in a completely disinterested manner. I booked a shared room. And this is by far, the worst hostel I’ve ever stayed in. Nothing beats this. Do yourself a favour and go for something different. Even something cheaper does a better job seriously.

Receptionist doesn’t not acknowledge customers. No welcome doesn’t even say a word. Card machine doesn’t work. The Wi-Fi was the slowest in Taipei. The bed had stains on it and the plug to charge electronics is by your feet. The washrooms were not clean, no toilet paper and had no hand soap.

They don't even provide hand soap in the washroom. The door is loud every time someone opens or closes it. I wore earbuds and could still hear it. They don't provide any amenities to you like towels. It's annoying to have to put in the room card so you can use the light or the outlet.

Go to Star Hostel instead. You can stay here if you really don't have any other options for your budget but it won't be an ideal experience.

reviews.text:
You get what you pay for

We booked the hotel because the price was cheap and the pictures looked good. First of all, it has to be said that the rooms don't look anywhere near as clean and well-kept and new as they do in the pictures. Everything is pretty worn out. You're used to that in Asia, but I'd still like to mention it.
Then it smelled very unpleasantly musty in the room, as there were no windows and the old carpeting certainly contributed to this. The air conditioning didn't seem to run continuously to compensate for this and the air conditioning filters didn't seem to have been changed/cleaned for a very long time.
In addition, it feels like the walls are made of paper and you can hear every conversation from the neighboring room. This was doubly unpleasant for us because the neighbors were partying, drinking and shouting all night long.
We checked out again after one night.

The rooms are dirty, moldy and has a strong scent of cigarettes even thou its a non smoking room.

The hotel is at the 10th floor. Below floors are karaoke, bar and casino - not safe since youll be sharing the lift with them.

Booked at January 10 but immediately checked out due to this. No refund.

If you are a new traveler, female and solo do not BOOK here, the photo they advertise is false and the high reviews does not reflect the true condition of the room!

Many flies in the room, at least 8 in both room and toilet. Called to feedback but he receptionist said can’t do anything because it’s late, can’t change room either because it’s full. He mentioned they spray the room everyday but I don’t believe so with the evidence of flies. So disgusting. Service of receptionist is rude. Never come back again. Hope google has 0 stars so I can give them 0 score.

Rebranded as LiHo Hotel or Moshamanla Hotel. All the same place. The good: great powerful shower, free bottled water daily, rooms made up daily. Huge flatscreen tv, mosquito nets on the windows.
The bad: the odour. You need to have the air conditioning on just to mask the smell.
The ugly: the place is filthy, the carpets sticky. Found toe nail clippings on the carpet.
Also, the pictures of the reception are not from this hotel which is misleading.

Multi tenant building. Careful: Very different to the pics they provided in bookings website.
Check in at 10th floor. Worth only for what you paid for. Suitable for solo trip with the least expectation you can get for a room
to sleep in only. Not much service / amenities. No toothbrush, slippers. Worn out ceilings. No cabinet. Only has hangers and clothes rack. Aesthetic wise definitely not what you would hope to see in a hotel but good enough just to sleep in after a day of tripping.

Pros:
Very convenient in Ximen town with convenience stores very nearby.

Cons:
Everything else about the room.

Solo trippers can consider without much expectations.

reviews.text:
We had a horrible experience at this place. I booked this place for my elderly parents who arrived from Europe after a very long and hard trip the same day. As my mother is claustrophobic and can‘t use elevator due to extreme fear of closed small spaces I asked during booking to put them on a lower floor. Also letting them know that she can’t use elevator.
As we arrived I again let them know about. They ended up giving a room on 7th floor and told us we are not allowed to use the stairs, only elevator. It is absolutely ridiculous!!! After a few arguments back and forth they basically told me to contact Agoda and cancel our booking and try to find another place. That after a 24 hour trip on a Taiwan Holiday when everything is booked out and super expensive!! So much for welcoming and friendly Taiwanese.
The cleanliness is superb👍🏻 satisfied with the hotel in overall except the location. It’s a bit far from the city, have to spend around 500twd for each trip

This was my first time in Taiwan, and I only speak English. The Fuji hotel was definitely 5 stars. The beds were very comfortable and the huge breakfasts were wonderful. After breakfast one morning our group took a taxi (which was coordinated by the Fuji staff) to and from Elephant Mountain, which was a great hike straight up many stairs to see a nice overlook of Taipei. The service at Fuji was excellent with comfortable places to sit and visit with friends in the grand lobby. The steam room, sauna & cold pool were a nice way to relax at the end of a long day hiking and seeing the city, and the gym facility was perfect for stretching in the morning. It was a short trip on the hotel shuttle to the MRT, which would take us to our next destination, which was the main Taipei train station. The whole trip was amazing, especially because most of our group only speak English. Also, we enjoyed going to Costco was right next door, which was very convenient to go shopping.
It's an average hotel but they could at least employ a bellboy to handle the luggage.

The hotel was good, service provided was also good. However nearby locations are only for Car sales or repairs. So nothing much other than Costco which needs a mebership card and you need to buy in large quantity.

The staff were friendly and very helpful. Had a personal issue (classic scenario of a tourist in a foreign country) on my first night at their hotel and the staff went beyond their duties to assist me resolve it. They were also able to fulfill my minor request via the application Line. The bread and coffee provision every morning was also greatly appreciated.
Like to stay this hotel because the room is clean and quiet. Only the metro station kind of distance to walk. I don't mind cause I treat it as exercise.

Not bad! Good cleaners, service.

If you're over 6 feet tall though, the shower will likely be too small so do keep that in mind. It's manageable still.

Room smells vaguely of cigarettes when we entered although there are no smoking signs prominently displayed. Air quality is bad enough to cause my throat to be scratchy, air conditioner also makes the air feel clammy. We booked for 3 nights, but made the decision to pack an overnight bag and left right away. Room was paid upfront with no chance of a refund. Had to skip around Taipei to find rooms for the night which proved challenging as Jay Chow had sold out concerts over the weekend. We checked out a day earlier this evening and the reception can’t be bothered to ask why. Never again.

reviews.text:
We self-checked in late at night and stayed for a few nights. This budget hostel offers a fantastic location, just a short walk from the Ximending Night Market and the MRT station.

Our room didn’t have a window, which made it a bit humid, but it was very clean overall. I appreciated the coffee and tea station in the common area, which added a nice touch to our stay.

I would recommend this place for anyone looking for affordability and convenience!

This is one of the cheapest places in the city center of Taipei. We stayed in a private room with a private shower The place was clean but a lot of things not working properly in the room. The air conditioning system smells bad when used for long, probably because it was a long time since it was cleaned well. The bathroom is big enough but the drainage in the shower was clogged. The disposable toiletries were very limited and no refills were given daily. The great thing here is the location. Near everything but still in a quiet area.

This is my first time staying in a hostel. And it feels like I'm back in college with dorm style living.

The hostel check in is located on the 4th floor. Easy check in process through the machine located right next to the elevator.

The living area is very cozy surprisingly. Nice ambiance with wood tones. Slippers are provided as well to wear while in the hostel. This is where the common area is for the kitchen, large table to work or hang out, washing room, and bathrooms. It's actually more clean than a hotel room because all the occupants are cleaning up after themselves.

I booked a room with a private bathroom. The room was spacious with its own fridge. The only compliant is that there are no electrical outlets right next to the bedside.

The AC was strong and there was also a window!

Window rooms are fully booked so I had 1 without window Pte room w bath, the bed is very comfortable, it is very quiet, it has Japanese toilet seat, big tv to update on typhoon situation, it has hot water dispenser, it has a common space where you can heat up food, great on a typhoon day!

But the bathroom at the common area, I think the dorms are using these bathrooms, are not clean and very dirty and smelly. So I will not stay at the dorm.

it would be perfect if it’s with windows, not to mentioned surrounded by good massage shop!

Love the self checking in process with the kiosk. It was a smooth process.

The room was ok. The bed was comfy, and the AC was strong. There was plenty of hot water, and the toilet was Western style.

There was no peeping hole on the door, which should be standard for the safety of the people inside the room. Further, an available door chain would have made us feel safer.

TV isn't smart. It's cable only.

There was construction going on behind the building, which woke us up in the morning, but it wasn't that bad.

There is a washer and a dryer downstairs and cost 50 NTD for the washing machine.  A 700-watt microwave, air fryer, and hot/cold water are available as well at the lobby.

reviews.text: Clean and simple, nothing fancy here. But, it's a 2 minute walk to the Taipei Main Station, so super-convenient for tourists wishing to travel around the city and indeed the country!

Location is great.  Just a few metres away from M8 access to Taipei Main Station. Easy to find food. Room is dated but alright.  No kettle in room but provided hot cold water dispenser near lift.  Our room has no view, only window looking out to air well. Bed is harder than my liking. Staff friendly and helpful.

The room is nice and the location is very accessible with 7-11 and Familymart nearby. There is also a 新光 nearby as well as various shops and of course Taipei main station which has HSR HRA and the Metro. There is an entrance to the station one block away. There is barely any amenities inside the hotel besides laundry 40nt for wash 20nt for dry but it barely dries. You can place your luggage in early before your check in time. Comes with 2 towels soap toothbrush comb shampoo body wash razor .

Very nice hotel near Taipei Main Station. Strategic location, 3min walk from M8 exit (with escalator) from Taipei Metro station.
Deluxe room is well equipped, with comfortable bed and electronic bidet toilet seat!
Normal twin bed room is less nice, the renovation is simple as compare to deluxe one.
Forgot to take my phone after checkout. Contacted them via email and they replied within short period of time. Yup, found back my phone as well.
Highly recommended this hotel.

I feel there is no hospitality among the staff. (Maybe it depends on the person.) I asked the front desk staff to arrange a taxi to the airport the next morning, but they refused, saying that you have to make the call. This is the only hotel in Taipei that refused to arrange a taxi. Also, I contacted them in advance in English, either by email or via the booking website, with an enquiry or request, I could not get a reply at all.

reviews.text:
The room is extremely narrow, and upon entering, there is an overwhelming musty odor. Black mold covers the walls, as well as the hairdryer, remote control, and showerhead.

There is a standalone split-type air conditioner, but it cannot be operated with the remote control. Worse yet, visible black mold is growing inside the unit.

Despite having an independent air conditioner, a strong cigarette smell periodically fills the room, likely seeping in through the bathroom’s ventilation system.

Soundproofing is practically nonexistent—you can clearly hear conversations, showers, and other noises from the neighboring rooms.

The door is very difficult to open, and it’s hard to tell if it has locked properly.
Cellular signals are terrible, and the Wi-fi  speed is sooo low, with huge ping and packet lost.

Water pressure is sufficient, which is a plus, but hot water sometimes takes up to 30 seconds to come through.

Absolutely filthy hairs all over the bed and floor not sure if the sheets had enough been changed there was also a big nail clipping on the floor staff aren't hoovering or cleaning just sitting outside in the hall playing loud music every morning from 7am there's a 2 inch gap under the door so you can hear everything the hotels has dampness in the rooms and rat traps in the hall far too expensive for what it is the only good point in the location

This seems very cheap love hotel.

Translucent bathroom sliding door, and smelly.
Our room at least has 3 different sizes cockroach, we went to the reception and ask what should we do, they said because I have only booked one night for the stay, so they won’t change the room to me, and just gave me a bugs killer spray, we are so scared for the whole night and can’t sleep well, all of our luggage not dare to open, NOT RECOMMENDED AT ALL.

If you’re trying to save money and want a place to stay that’s near the station. Don’t stay here.
Stay somewhere else. I’ve had 13 bug bites in our 3 night stay in this place. I wish we had just paid more money somewhere else with a comfortable and clean bed.

Additionally, everything looks old. The place was not nice and tidy compared from where I stayed in Taichung. There’s not much room to move around, and there’s two of us staying in one room and my partner is 6’3.

There is NO KETTLE to make coffee in the room. It’s in the lobby area on the first floor.

AC is working fine but the interior is just old and horrible looking. I feel like there are cockroaches around when we sleep.

Cosmo Hotel is conveniently located near Taipei Main Station (50 metres to nearest M3 entrance/exit) making it a great choice for easy access to transportation and exploring the city.

I represent a group of 50+ people, some with special needs, staying at Cosmos Hotel Taipei from 1 Dec to 4 Dec.

Claire, the Sales Manager, has been extremey patient with our communications, catering to the needs of our special needs from the start.

Shane, the Front Desk Officer, shown great empathy and understanding towards our group the moment we arrived and until we left.

reviews.text:
Nice hotel in great location. Minutes from MRT station and there was bus stop just across the road. We had requested a quiet room and they provided just that. Staffs are very attentive and helpful to the best of their ability.

Also loving the washing-drying facilities they have. Very reasonable price and it's so good to have fresh clean clothes done inside the hotel instead of having to walk around looking for a coin laundry. Hopefully they will have more washer/dryer machine as the machines (2 pairs) are always in use!

It's not near a MRT station, but there is a bus stop in front of the hotel. The rooms are clean and somewhat new, however they are similar to the compacted Japanese hotel rooms. The breakfasts tasty decent, but options are somewhat limited and they serve the same food everyday. There is no gym in the building. At their price point, I will likely find a different hotel that is closer to the MRT the next time I visit.

This review is based on the value of the property for the price we paid (~$3600NTD/night on avg)

Firstly, we booked an accessibility/king bed room in the 11th floor. The room was very small, basically the door opens and the bed is right in front, but it was liveable. The room included a humble sized closet, mini fridge, small desk, and tv. The washroom, however, was about the same size as the room itself. We had two strollers that took up the entire "empty" space that was available between the entryway and desk. In sum, a small room but it worked.

The washroom is the no divider style, unless you use the bathtub which we did not want to use. The sink does not come with a vanity, so it was just a sink and no countertop space for anything else. Less functional, but still we made it work. Toilet, sink, and shower all worked just fine. However, the ventilation is extremely poor. Basically everything we hung in the washroom dried poorly.

The bed was comfortable, HOWEVER, I do suspect "uncleanliness" (dust? Others?) because we (2 adults+2 toddlers) all had a couple/few very small red bumps that don't look or itch the same way as mosquito bites. This is my biggest concern and reflected in my rating.

Otherwise, we thoroughly enjoyed the complimentary breakfast over our 15 night stay. Food was fresh and tasty. Although, on the last few days the daily veggies went from cabbage to bean sprouts. The kitchen staff was friendly, hardworking, and there to deliver a great service every single day. We miss them!

The only thing I did voice directly to staff is concern about the safety of the accessibility ramp to the lobby. It is located off to the side of the staircased main entrance. Most nights, the light for this ramp entrance was off. It was dark until you fully stepped into the lobby. Occasionally, the light was on. We pushed strollers with toddlers and never felt unsafe, mostly because my husband was always around. However the experience could be very different for others.

Staff said the light is controlled by the restaurant, so it depends on the restaurant and they - the hotel - have no control. This was an unacceptable answer to me. The accessibility ramp is part of the hotel entrance, then the light should be part of the hotel's accessibility and safety considerations, not left to the restaurant. I hope management can take this into serious reconsideration; it should not be a complicated issue to resolve.

Overall, would recommend:)

reviews.text:
People were singing until 5 AM—I could hear everything, from the bass and guitar to the melody of their voices. When my neighbors took a shower in the middle of the night, I could hear the sound of the water running and the faucet turning on.

One incident that almost turned into a bad experience was when I forgot my valuable item in my room before checking out. I clearly remember placing it on the table as the last thing to pack because I was afraid it might break. That’s why I forgot it.

After leaving the city, I had to come all the way back to the hotel, put on gloves, and dig through the trash in every room. It smelled terrible. But in the end, the housekeeper suddenly “remembered” that they had kept it safe for me.

I’m not sure if it was just a coincidence that they were exhausted from work and forgot they had kept my item, or if they had intended to “forget” it. But seeing my determination to search through the trash, they finally decided to return it to me.

Either way, thank you.

This hotel was horrible!
I stayed in this hotel in the very dirty building with my parents. We all couldn’t sleep during the night because of the noise from KTV and outside the room. We couldn’t rest at all although all we needed was good rest during the trip. The room didn’t smell clean and the shower room wasn’t nice because the water didn’t drain well…
This kind of hotel shouldn’t be operated. I felt like I was sleeping on the street. The rating on booking.com seemed ok so I booked here, but I won’t recommend this hotel to anyone by all means.

reviews.text:
Caesar Metro Taipei offers a seamless and convenient stay.
The location makes commuting effortless.
The rooms are clean, decent sized and well-maintained, providing a comfortable environment for a restful stay.
Service was exceptional; staff were helpful and friendly.
Staff members like Dennis and Alain at Concierge were very responsive, and went the extra mile to ensure a smooth experience. Their exemplary service, attentiveness and professionalism are simply commendable.

The hotel has a nice lobby- but they are very strict about not eating or drinking while waiting.
The rooms are adequate — bigger than the ones in XiMenDing.
The toilet is a little tight. Needs extra leg space.
Water dispenser is available at every floor- much better for the environment.
During peak times, the elevator takes a while to arrive. And sometimes, it arrives full of people.
Bed is firm and comfortable. Aircon works well.
Staff are efficient.

A quiet hotel. It has an expansive buffet (added charge 4 stars). The rooms are smallish, especially by American standards but are very modern and well laid out (4 stars). The Gym is lacking, no weight equipment though they have lots of space  (1+ star). At peak times, the elevators, though very modern are saturated. The only thing I REALLY didn’t like was the lobby music which also played in the dining area. A short 2 minute high pitched repeating violin “tune”. Very irritating after the first day. Location was good with a well stocked 7/11 across the street (1/2L Tiger beer for about $1.40, 12 oz Kirin for 90 cents and 1/2 L Coke for 80 cents).

All the staff were friendly, and the front desk employees spoke English well, so there were no communication issues. It was convenient to store luggage during check-in and check-out. The hotel’s location was also very convenient for traveling. The room condition was very clean, and the bed was especially comfortable for sleeping. Also, the room was spacious, which made it easy to spread out and organize my belongings. The room was really soundproof, so I slept very well.

However, I stayed at this accommodation twice for two nights each, and in the room I was assigned on the second stay (17th floor), the drainage didn’t work well, causing water to overflow outside the shower area.

We got there 2 hrs earlier than the check in time. So my family had to wait in the lobby after a long flight from SFO. The minute we walked in the lobby, we can smell people smoking in the area. There were a lot of people waiting. While we were waiting, my son closed his eyes in the chair nearby because of the jet leg. A staff came by told him that he is not allowed to take nap in the lobby. The staff also walked around to make sure no one is taking naps or taking their shoes off. I guess that are the  rules for the hotel.

reviews.text: It was an incredible experience and well enjoyed by our family. The pool is warmed great for the spring weather. Security and hospitality are spot on. The gym space is nice with lots of equipment options. I was on the treadmill with the view of the bustling streets and World Trade Center. The location of the hotel is in a convenient location to nearby tourist attractions. There is a sky bridge right off the side entrance that reaches Taipei 101. Again, all the staff was very friendly and helped meet our accommodation requests prior to our visit. My children loved the space we had in our room. We got a 2 twin bed room with a sofa bed for us four.

I stayed at the Grand Hyatt Taipei for 6 nights, and overall, it was a great experience. The hotel’s location is hard to beat – it’s right next to Taipei 101 and just steps away from Exit 5 of the metro, making it incredibly easy to get around the city. Whether you’re heading to the 101 or exploring other parts of Taipei, everything is within walking distance, which was a huge plus.

The hotel has the classic grand entrance you’d expect from a Hyatt, giving it a sophisticated and welcoming vibe. My room was nice, though I did feel the ceiling was a bit low, which made the space feel a little more confined than I expected. However, the room was well-appointed with standout features like an Illy Francisco coffee machine—definitely a highlight for me as a coffee lover—and a separate bed and sofa area, which made the room feel spacious enough to relax after a long day.

The views from the room were good, but with Taipei 101 being so close, I felt like it was almost too close for the ideal cityscape shot. It’s a cool view, but you do feel like you’re right under it.

As for the service, it was top-notch. The customer service was excellent, and the staff were always friendly and helpful. The breakfast spread was plentiful, offering a wide variety of choices to suit different tastes.

I also had access to the Grand Club Lounge, which was decent for a quick snack or a drink, though it’s more basic in terms of offerings.

All in all, the Grand Hyatt Taipei is a solid choice, especially if you’re looking for a hotel with a prime location and comfortable amenities.

Grand Hyatt Taipei – A Wonderful Stay!

I had a fantastic stay at Grand Hyatt Taipei and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting the city.
•	Room & Comfort: The room was spacious, clean, and well-equipped, providing a very comfortable stay.
•	Service: The service was exceptional—fast, efficient, and everyone was incredibly helpful. The staff was genuinely friendly and made the experience even more enjoyable.
•	Dining: Breakfast was excellent, with a wide variety of options to choose from. The quality of food and selection made for a great start to the day.
•	Facilities: I didn’t use the gym, pool, or spa, so I can’t comment on them.
•	Location: Perfect for both sightseeing and business. The hotel is conveniently located near shopping malls, Taipei 101, Breeze Center, and the MRT, making it easy to get around.
•	Overall Impression: Totally worth the price! I would definitely stay here again.

Big hotel at a convenient location next to shopping and restaurants area, next to Taipei 101 and metro station.

Excessive breakfast with Western, Asian and  Japanese options, eggs station and bakery.

Spacious gym with 3 areas: free weights, yoga/anaerobic, cardio and cable machines. Sauna access is included. Massage options.

Rooms are spacious, clean and well equipped.

Definitely recommend, especially for business trips.

I had a wonderful time at the Grand Hyatt! It’s an oldie but a well-maintained goodie. Staff were all amazing, friendly yet professional. The buffet was so tasty and had a good variety. The rooms were clean and as we stayed twice this time, got to see the slightly layouts of the rooms but the view of 101 was, in both stays, amazing. We also tried their outdoor heated pool which was really good given it’s winter. The location was also unbeatable. It was a great stay!
